NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 9 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 8 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 3, 12:36 PM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 9 DraftKings main slate at 19.1 DraftKings points for $7,700, at Seattle. Brock Bowers (15.3, $7,900) and George Kittle (12.5, $6,000) are next.

Greg Dulcich returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.88 projected points per $1,000 at $3,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 3, 12:36 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 9

Trey McBride, ARI at SEA ($7,700)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 19.1 DraftKings points at $7,700. That is 3.8 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 11.5 targets on 41.7 routes. The salary works out to 2.48 projected points per $1,000, 3rd of 16 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 19.0 points with a simulated floor of 4.9 and a ceiling of 45.8, and he holds 6% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 10.5-point underdog on the road against Seattle, with an implied team total of 16 in a game totaled at 42.5.

Brock Bowers, LV at SF ($7,900)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 15.3 DraftKings points at $7,900. The model gives him 8.4 targets on 32.8 routes. The salary works out to 1.94 projected points per $1,000, 14th of 16 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 15.4 points with a simulated floor of 3.2 and a ceiling of 41.6, and he holds 3% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 10-point underdog on the road against San Francisco, with an implied team total of 20.75 in a game totaled at 51.5.

Value: Greg Dulcich, MIA vs DET ($3,100)

Greg Dulcich projects for 8.9 DraftKings points at $3,100, which works out to 2.88 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 16 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.4 targets on 18.5 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Dulcich averaged 8.9 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 30.9, and he holds 18% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 7-point underdog at home against Detroit, with an implied team total of 21.75 in a game totaled at 50.5.
